subject: a command-line tool that counts log entries per level and per component
conclusion: logtally reads each file once, keeps the entries that pass one filter, counts them by one key and prints the counts.
why: One pass over each file keeps memory flat. The parser counts a malformed line and reports it, so a bad line never stops the count.

glossary.definition: one parsed log line: a timestamp, a level, a component and a message
the number the tool returns to the shell when it stops

flow.title: From log files to counts
flow.text: A staged process: each step hands its output to the next step, then the run ends with an exit status.

items.label: Options
items.desc: The entry point reads the file names and the options from the command line.

items.label: Parse
items.desc: The parser reads each file once and turns every line into an entry or a skipped count.

items.label: Filter
items.desc: One combined test drops entries below the level floor or before the start time.

items.label: Count
items.desc: The counter groups the kept entries by level or by component, highest count first.

items.label: Print
items.desc: A renderer prints the counts as an aligned table or as JSON.

items.label: Exit status
items.desc: The tool returns 2 when it skipped malformed lines and 0 when every line parsed.

facts.text: A usage error returns exit status 64.
The log format is a timestamp, a level, a bracketed component and a message.

inferred: Memory use grows with the number of kept entries, not with the size of the files.

lines.name: read-options

lines.name: parse-and-filter

lines.name: count-and-print

scenes.title: What the exit status tells you

lines.name: clean-run

lines.name: skipped-lines
